# Saved records and artifacts

The descriptions are maintained in `docs/formats.toml`; implementation locations are listed below.
See the [constructor reference](models.md) for parameter names and defaults, [options](options.md)
for solver settings, and [results](results.md) for the structure of result objects in memory.

## Common scalar result envelope

Implementation: `src/qdjj_solver/common/io.py: result_record; qp_solver/io.py; dmrg_solver/io.py`.

save_result supports static QP and DMRG eigenstates. It writes JSON with format='qdjj-eigenstates', format_version=1 and backend='qp' or 'dmrg', and returns None. Scalar JSON can be analysed with ordinary JSON tools; load_result additionally requires a state artifact.

### `format`

Literal 'qdjj-eigenstates'.

### `format_version`

Integer 1.

### `backend`

'qp' or 'dmrg'; selects the loader and backend-specific metadata.

### `energies`

One real many-body energy per state in the declared Hamiltonian reference. Obtain excitation gaps by taking energy differences.

### `residuals`

One residual norm per state; DMRG can use null when residual evaluation was disabled.

### `observables`

Mapping from observable name to one value per state, using complex encoding where necessary.

### `timings_seconds`

Named elapsed-time measurements, with method-dependent keys; use them to assess computational cost in the recorded environment.

### `calculation`

The result object's metadata dictionary, stored under the key calculation: settings, sector and diagnostics.

### `environment`

Package/library versions, Python, platform and machine information.

### `implementation`

Imported implementation version, portable relative file hashes and their aggregate SHA256.

### `hamiltonian_sha256`

Fingerprint of the complete Hamiltonian record.

### `hamiltonian`

Full Hamiltonian record in standard save_result output. The lower-level record helper can omit it; retain it for state restoration.

### `qp_weights`

QP only: state-by-bath-QP-number probabilities, with shape (states, cutoff+1).

### `state_artifact`

Present only when states are saved; kind, format_version, file and sha256 identify the companion.

### `state_amplitudes`

QP saves also retain the legacy file/sha256 companion descriptor.

## QP calculation metadata

Implementation: `src/qdjj_solver/qp_solver/solver.py`.

The QP calculation copies the model metadata and adds the following fields. Additional method-specific diagnostics may also be present; this dictionary is extensible.

### `sector`

All four Sector fields.

### `qp_cutoff`

Resolved integer bath-QP cutoff.

### `dimension`

Number of retained Fock basis states.

### `bath_modes`

Number of declared non-impurity modes.

### `impurity_modes`

Number of impurity spin modes.

### `method`

Selected eigensolver method after automatic dispatch.

### `options`

Resolved SolverOptions dictionary.

### `basis_bytes`

Native basis storage estimate in bytes.

### `estimated_solver_bytes`

Estimated solver storage in bytes; actual process memory also includes allocations outside this estimate.

### `real_arithmetic`

Whether the projected calculation used real arithmetic.

### `nnz`

Stored sparse entry count if available, otherwise null.

## DMRG calculation metadata

Implementation: `src/qdjj_solver/dmrg_solver/solver.py`.

The finite-problem convergence flag requires satisfactory residuals, stable sweep energies, energy ordering and orthogonality. Assess bath convergence by refinement, and check the completeness of the low-energy spectrum through additional state searches or an independent reference.

### `backend`

Literal 'dmrg'.

### `tenpy`

TeNPy version used.

### `options`

Resolved DMRG SolverOptions.

### `sector`

Selected Sector fields.

### `qp_cutoff`

Null: DMRG retains all QP numbers allowed by the declared model and sector.

### `bath_modes`

Declared non-impurity mode count.

### `impurity_modes`

Impurity spin-mode count.

### `mode_order`

Canonical mode permutation along the MPS.

### `groups`

Modes assigned to each MPS site.

### `coordinate_id`

Physical-coordinate and layout fingerprint.

### `energy_reference`

Description inherited from the Hamiltonian, or 'as specified in Hamiltonian'.

### `restriction`

Any declared dark-mode restriction inherited from model construction; DMRG acts on the retained modes.

### `search_energy_shift`

Scalar search shift used during excited-state optimization.

### `operator_norm_bound`

Operator-coefficient norm bound used in the search.

### `mpo_dimensions`

Physical MPO bond dimensions, or null for a zero operator.

### `mpo_original_dimensions`

Dimensions before exact parallel-channel merging, or null.

### `search_shift_bound`

Method used to choose the search bound, or null.

### `roots`

Optimization diagnostics for each state, including independent trials, sweep histories, actual bond dimensions and stopping information.

### `gram`

Full state overlap matrix, bra rows and ket columns.

### `gram_error`

Norm of the deviation of gram from the identity.

### `roots_energy_ordered`

Whether the retained eigenstates are ordered by energy.

### `residual_method`

'untruncated-(H-E)-MPS-QR' when residuals are evaluated, otherwise null.

### `finite_problem_converged`

Combined finite-Hamiltonian convergence assessment.

### `bath_convergence_checked`

False: bath convergence requires a separate study.

## DMRG root and trial diagnostics

Implementation: `src/qdjj_solver/dmrg_solver/solver.py`.

Each calculation.roots entry describes the selected candidate for one eigenstate. Iteratively obtained states include sweep and trial data; exact single-site and zero-operator solutions have shorter records.

### `sweep_converged`

TeNPy's combined energy/entropy stopping flag, separate from the full finite-problem assessment.

### `sweep_energy_converged`

Stability of the last three sweep energies within four times energy_tolerance.

### `sweeps`

Number of optimization sweeps; zero for exact special cases.

### `chi_actual`

Largest actual MPS bond dimension; one for exact single-site/zero-operator cases.

### `seed`

Product-state indices, 'continuation', an excitation-operator/source-root object, or randomized-seed details. Absent for exact special cases.

### `lower_root_overlap`

Largest magnitude of the overlap amplitude with a previously calculated eigenstate; absent for exact special cases.

### `norm_error`

Norm of TeNPy's canonical-form diagnostic; absent for exact special cases.

### `sweep_statistics`

TeNPy per-sweep arrays; non-finite diagnostics are encoded as null. Names depend on the installed TeNPy version.

### `seed_trials`

List of attempted candidates, each with energy, sweep_converged, lower_root_overlap and seed; empty for exact special cases.

### `method`

Present for exact special cases: 'single-site-exact' or 'zero-operator'.

## Companion wavefunctions

Implementation: `src/qdjj_solver/qp_solver/io.py; src/qdjj_solver/dmrg_solver/io.py`.

Keep the JSON record and its named companion file in the same directory. Saving uses unique companion filenames and replaces the JSON record atomically. Obtain the companion filename from the JSON record's state_artifact.file field.

### `kind`

'fock-amplitudes-npz' or 'tenpy-mps-hdf5'.

### `format_version`

Companion descriptor version 1.

### `file`

Basename of the companion file in the result directory.

### `sha256`

Checksum of the companion bytes, checked before loading.

### `NPZ`

energies, vectors (basis rows, eigenstate columns), occupations (uint64 word rows), qp_counts, result_sha256. The last binds the scalar record; older four-array files remain readable.

### `HDF5`

TeNPy data containing format='qdjj-mps', format_version=1, coordinate_id, result_sha256 and states. Load trusted MPS artifacts with compatible TeNPy/HDF5 support.

### `validation`

Loaders check format, checksum, Hamiltonian and coordinate/basis identities, shapes and state consistency. Editing scalar records can invalidate their binding to wavefunctions.

### `legacy-QP`

format='bcs-qp-eigenstates', version 1, is also readable. It uses state_amplitudes and lacks the common backend/provenance envelope. New unified saves use the common format.

## Model and spectral records

Implementation: `common/baths.py; common/problem.py; common/floquet.py; common/spectra.py`.

Each object's record() method provides the fields listed below for explicit JSON encoding of arrays and complex values. These records describe models, drives and spectral lines; save_result and load_result handle static eigenstates and their companion wavefunctions.

### `DiscreteBath`

xi, weights, delta, bandwidth, metadata. from_record reconstructs and validates coefficients.

### `Hamiltonian`

operator, nimp, spins, eta_labels, observables, metadata. Operators are serialized term lists; the additive constant is retained.

### `Harmonic`

order, amplitude, phase.

### `ParameterDrive`

parameter, index, harmonics (Harmonic records).

### `PeriodicHamiltonian`

omega, nimp, spins, eta_labels, harmonics (string nonnegative indices to operator lists), reference (Hamiltonian record), observables (signed harmonic keys), metadata.

### `SpectralLines`

frequencies, strengths, final, initial, photons, elastic, metadata. Merged initial/final index lists and population-weighted strengths retain their interpretation.
